fields.v: TDAD + Claude Code (version n.s.) + Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) for all roles; Built Agent run with Claude Agent SDK. Criterion stated by the authors per run: compilation success (all visible tests pass within 6 outer / 8 inner iterations); HPR, MS and SURS reported without a target. Values (Tables 4-5, successful runs): v1 compile 11/12 (92%), HPR 97.3±2.6%, MS 95.9±7.1%, cost $2.32±0.96, 3.1±0.8 iterations; v2 compile 7/12 (58%), HPR 77.7±13.9% (lowest 51.1%), MS 100%, SURS 97.2±3.5%, cost $2.81±1.71, 2.9±1.1 iterations; total $45.15 for 18 successful runs. Quality: no configuration-level criterion stated by the authors (per-run compilation criterion met in 11/12 v1 and 7/12 v2 runs). Cost: no criterion stated by the authors ($2-3 per spec version, called 'potentially prohibitive for rapid prototyping')
fields.quote: A single spec version takes 30– 60 minutes wall-clock and $2–3 in API costs, comparable to CI/CD pipeline times but potentially prohibitive for rapid prototyping.
fields.why: The verdicts 'works (v1), partly (v2)' and cost 'works' rest on thresholds chosen by the extractor; the authors state only a per-run compilation criterion and no cost criterion (rule of 2026-11-23).
fields.doubt: Os autores não dão critério de sucesso para o custo nem para a configuração no todo; só o critério por execução (compilar = passar todos os testes visíveis). Pela regra de 23-11, o veredicto deve ser 'no criterion stated by the authors' (como fizeste no CodeCompass). Vê pág. 6-7 e decide.

fields.v: Spec-as-source (not stated in Böckeler terms). Authors: 'The specification is the single source of truth. Tests implement the specification; they don't define it'; the prompt is a 'compiled artifact' produced from the spec by PromptSmith and never edited by hand; v2 is compiled from the v1 artefact against the v2 tests
fields.quote: The specification is the single source of truth.
fields.why: The author's value is still marked '(draft, to check)', so the SDD level is not settled; the text supports spec-as-source but v2 builds on the v1 artefact, which a reader could call spec-anchored.
fields.doubt: O valor ainda diz '(draft, to check)'. O artigo trata a spec como única fonte e o prompt como artefacto compilado (pág. 1 e 3), o que aponta para spec-as-source; mas a v2 parte do prompt da v1 (pág. 5). Decide o nível e tira a nota de rascunho.
